concept.name: Trailing stop order
concept.definition: A stop order (or stop-limit order) whose stop price is not fixed but is set as a specified dollar amount or percentage away from the market price. As the price moves in the trader's favor the stop price trails it by that amount; if the price moves adversely the stop price stays fixed, and it triggers a market (or limit) order once reached.
concept.intuition: It is a stop-loss that ratchets: it follows the market when the market moves your way and never moves back, so it locks in progressively more of a favorable move without capping further gains.
concept.mechanics: The broker or venue recomputes the trigger as the extreme favorable price plus/minus the trailing amount; for a sell trailing stop the trigger equals the highest price since submission minus the trail amount. Triggering conventions differ by venue: some trigger on last-sale prices, others on quotation prices. Once triggered, a plain trailing stop becomes a market order, a trailing stop-limit becomes a limit order.
concept.formula: Sell trailing stop trigger = max(market price since order placement) - trailing amount (fixed $ or %). Buy trailing stop trigger = min(market price since order placement) + trailing amount.
concept.failure_modes: In a gap or fast market the triggered market order can fill far away from the trailing stop price, so the 'locked-in' level is not guaranteed. Short-term noise can also trigger the stop prematurely, whipsawing the trader out of a position.
concept.misconceptions: A trailing stop does not guarantee an exit at the trailing stop price - it is a trigger, not an execution price. It also does not protect against overnight gaps, since it can only trigger while the market is trading.
concept.example: You buy XYZ at $20 and place a sell trailing stop $1 below the market. XYZ peaks at $24 and falls; the trigger ratchets up to $23 and stays there, and the shares are sold (at or near $23) when the price trades down to $23.

citations.source: SEC Investor Bulletin: Understanding Order Types
citations.section: Stop, Stop-Limit, and Trailing Stop Orders
